topology_reasoning.identified_device: A compact, symmetric multi-rail folded delay/interconnect layout: five narrow through rails occupy the middle, while matching upper and lower five-rail banks fold at both ends around broad return rails.
topology_reasoning.operation: The repeated rounded end transitions route parallel optical traces between the narrow rail banks and the broader return regions while preserving ordered, constant-pitch channels across the 120 um active span.
observed_structure: five approximately 0.066 um-wide central horizontal rails at roughly 0.10 um pitch
five matching narrow rails in each upper and lower bank
one broad approximately 0.47 um return rail per upper/lower bank
symmetric rounded, tapered end transitions beginning about 8 um from each end
topology_reasoning.implementation_plan: Assemble all material from GDSFactory straight, rectangle, taper, and gf.Path/extrude primitives. Use rounded U-like transition centerlines for narrow bank rails and broad Path/extrude return rails. delta_length will extend one real narrow arm and be measured from that arm path in lengths.json.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitives-only assembly. The long bank rails and broad return rails match the central span closely; the diff shows central through rails are about 0.012 um low and end fan-outs need refinement.
Tested a +0.012 um global middle-rail shift. It worsened overlap substantially because the existing alignment was already correct to the raster grid; reverted before the next topology change.

Replaced the incorrect center-connected fan-outs with separate five-rail banks, compact tapered bank feeders, and measured steep-to-shallow broad-return transitions. This is the retained best and exceeds the 0.85 Phase-A threshold.
Rewrote the GDS without metadata context so the physical cell remains top-level for deterministic layer-area verification; geometry and visual metrics are unchanged.
